questions.prompt: agent-2 read task-1 at revision 1, but agent-1 has since claimed it. What happens when agent-2 claims with expectedRevision 1?
options: The claim fails because the current revision is 2
agent-1 loses the task to agent-2
The board waits until agent-1 finishes
questions.explanation: Compare-and-set changes the task only if its revision still equals what the caller read. It is now 2, so the claim throws.

questions.prompt: Why does every change increase the revision by one?
options: So an agent can tell that a task changed after it read it
So the board can count how many agents exist
So old tasks are deleted after ten changes
So the model knows how long a task took
questions.explanation: A new revision on every change means a stale read always shows a different number, and the check catches it.

questions.prompt: The lead adds a task that agent-1 should start. What must the lead also do?
options: Nothing, because the board wakes every member
Send agent-1 a message, because a board change wakes nobody
Restart agent-1 so it reads the board
Claim the task for agent-1 and complete it
questions.explanation: Board changes do not add inbox messages or start idle agents, so the lead sends an explicit message.
